systems.name: KotlinBottools
systems.function: A Kotlin Discord bot framework on JDA: hierarchical text and slash commands, XML-backed guild and member data, event responders and polling services, built by one Gradle build at 7.5-SNAPSHOT.

systems.name: Toolchain
systems.function: Install, verify and pin every tool, and prove each check is not blind before it is trusted.

plannedBy.placement: WS/tools and the user-scheme pip install, outside every repository

systems.name: Backups and manifests
systems.function: Take one untouched mirror per repository and derive from it everything the rewrite is judged against.

plannedBy.placement: WS/backup and DATA/manifests, outside every repository

systems.name: Legacy data copy
systems.function: Preserve BotData.xml and guildData/ byte-exactly from three revisions before anything is rewritten.

systems.name: Rewrite pipeline
systems.function: Turn one backup-mirrored repository into a pushed, proven, rewritten repository, or stop before its push.

plannedBy.placement: WS/mirror, WS/fresh and DATA/rewrite, outside every repository

systems.name: Privacy gate and id-reference check
systems.function: Prove, by count, that nothing that becomes public with KotlinBottools names a guild, a member or a legacy id, and that nothing new cites a pre-rewrite id.

plannedBy.placement: WS/tools and DATA/run/gate, outside every repository

systems.name: Residual-exposure measurement
systems.function: Measure what GitHub still serves of each old history and report it in counts.

systems.name: Cleanup
systems.function: Leave the machine with the data folder and records, the two realigned clones, and nothing else of the phase.

plannedBy.placement: WS and DATA, outside every repository

systems.name: Repository swap
systems.function: Make the rewritten KotlinBottools public as a fresh repository without losing a number or a link.

systems.name: Clone realignment
systems.function: Bring this working directory onto the rewritten history in place, so that no push from it can carry old history, and replace the private repository clone with a fresh one at the same path.

plannedBy.placement: this working directory, the local private repository clone and the old clone's folder beside it on its own volume, and DATA/run/realign

systems.name: Repository hygiene
systems.function: The repository's own guard against committing secrets and data again: a root-anchored .gitignore, .gitleaks.toml with one scoped allowlist table, and the Secret scan workflow with its scan wrapper and the allowlist controls that test that table.

systems.name: Internal Tooling
systems.function: The tooling that runs the Phase 0 history rewrite from this repository, in four groups: the workspace's lifecycle, the rewrite and cut-over, the exposure proofs, and the repository's hygiene files.

systems.name: Workspace lifecycle
systems.function: Prepare the ground before anything is rewritten and clear it afterwards: pinned tools, untouched backups and the preserved data in, the workspace out.

systems.name: Rewrite and cut-over
systems.function: Replace the old histories and move everything onto them: each repository rewritten and proven, KotlinBottools made public as a fresh repository, the local clones realigned.

systems.name: Exposure proof
systems.function: Say by count what is exposed: that what becomes public names nothing it should not, and what GitHub still serves of each old history.

systems.name: Command model
systems.function: Turn an immutable command definition into a slash registration, a typed parser and generated help, and run one handler per invocation through one context.

systems.name: Bot runtime
systems.function: Own start-up and shutdown, the coroutine scope, the gateway, event routing, plugin installation, jobs and configuration.

systems.name: Storage
systems.function: Define the snowflake-keyed ports every stored thing goes through, ship an in-memory implementation, and the durable SQLite one with migrations, backups and atomic erasure.

plannedBy.placement: bottools-core (the ports and the in-memory implementation) and bottools-data-sqlite

systems.name: Outbound HTTP
systems.function: Own the call surface every provider and plugin programs against, and adapt it, internally, onto WebTools' HTTP stack.

systems.name: Stats framework
systems.function: Give every game provider a capability-based SPI, account links, a match tracker and a news feed over an ApiClient, and build the standard game commands from a provider's capabilities.

systems.name: Plugins
systems.function: Deliver the five 1.0.0 features as plugins over the runtime's contracts: reaction roles, math, admin, weather and feeds.

systems.name: Build and CI skeleton
systems.function: The multi-module build, convention plugins, test-set tasks, the documentation, ABI, classpath-alignment, release-metadata and secret-scanning gates, the WebTools composite with its published lane, and the release path.
